verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for the last three days and going to the toilet six or seven times a day with loose, watery stool: "I've just had some diarrhea for the last three days" and "probably like six or seven times a day... it's like loose and watery stool."
Patient describes stools as loose, watery, and explicitly denies blood: "it's like loose and watery stool" and "No, no blood, yeah, just watery and loose stool."

Patient has lower abdominal pain on the left side, crampy, intermittent, and non-radiating: "in my lower abdomen... just to one side... on the left side"; "it feels, um, like a cramp"; "it comes and goes"; and when asked if it moves, patient replies "no, just maybe my stomach." LLQ is a standard clinical inference for left lower abdominal pain.
Patient vomited at the start of symptoms and has now stopped: "I vomited at the start of the symptoms but now um I've stopped vomiting."

Patient reports feeling hot at onset, did not measure temperature, and currently denies fever: "I did notice um a temperature when the symptoms started"; "I didn't mention my temperature, no, but I felt, um, just a bit hot"; and "I haven't had a fever, um, at the moment." This supports a subjective fever at onset and currently afebrile by report.

Patient feels weak and shaky, has loss of appetite, but is tolerating fluids and mainly soups/smoothies: "yeah i feel a bit uh weak and shaky"; "I had a loss of appetite... but I've been able to hold down fluids"; and "just soups, and, uh, yeah, light foods. Like smoothies and, yeah, liquid foods mainly."

Patient reports having takeaway 4 days ago at a Chinese restaurant, queried as possible trigger: "I had takeaway about four days ago" and "I ate at a Chinese restaurant with friends"; doctor links this temporally to onset: "you mentioned you had this Chinese takeaway as little as three days ago and I wondered whether that might be the cause of your problems."
Patient has asthma and says it is under control: "other than um athsma, um I use an inhaler" and "yeah, that's fine. I just, yeah, use an inhaler, and uh that's under control."
Patient uses an inhaler, but no further details are given: "I use an inhaler" and later "I just, yeah, use an inhaler" with no type/dose specified.
Patient works as an accountant and lives with wife and two children: "I'm an accountant" and doctor confirms "you live with your wife and two children, is that right?" Patient answers, "Yes, yeah."
Patient is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol: "do you smoke at all?" – "no, I don't smoke"; "do you drink much in the way of alcohol?" – "no, I I don't drink alcohol, no."

Doctor diagnoses gastroenteritis and mentions viral/bacterial (foodborne) causes: "it seems like you may have something, uh, called gastroenteritis" and "Mainly caused by viruses but there can be a possibility of bacteria uh causing its symptoms." The timing with Chinese takeaway makes a foodborne cause a reasonable direct inference.

Doctor recommends Dioralyte but does not formally prescribe it or specify dosing: "there are things like Dioralyte you can get from the pharmacy" and "I would say recommend that in the first... couple of days." The phrase "Prescribed ... as directed" and implication of a formal prescription are not stated.

While the patient reports eating soups and light foods, the doctor does not explicitly advise "small frequent fluids and bland/light foods"; only hydration and Dioralyte are recommended: "making sure you're well hydrated, so drinking fluids" and discussion of Dioralyte. Specific dietary advice is not documented.

Doctor advises paracetamol but does not state dose, frequency in mg, or maximum daily dose: "taking some paracetamol, uh, two tablets up to four times a day." The fact's specification of "1 g every 6 hours, maximum 4 g/day" adds dosing details not given.

Doctor explicitly recommends rest and 2–3 days off work: "I will certainly advise you to take some time off work... I would say the next two, two to three days as the infection clears from your system to take some time off and rest."

The transcript does not contain specific red-flag or safety-net advice regarding dehydration, fever thresholds, bloody stools, severe pain, 7-day duration, or inability to tolerate oral intake. These details are not mentioned.

Doctor advises follow-up in 3–4 days if not better and mentions stool tests if ongoing: "if your symptoms haven't got better, you know, in in three to four days, I'd like to come and see you again" and "if it is ongoing... we may need to do further tests like um taking a sample of your stool so we can test that."
